value_stream.name: Employee Accommodation, Dormitory & Staff Housing Operations

fields.Participants: Housing Ops, HR (VS-103), Facilities (VS-138), Security (VS-23), Resident
fields.Volume: Per-site daily ops × ~housed-sites; check-in/out on assignment/move-out

workflows.name: Dormitory Daily Operations, Check-In/Out & Front-Desk Management

Automation Opportunity: - Digital check-in/out with assignment verification; access-card issuance; daily-occupancy auto-reconcile to HRIS
Controls: - CTL-663 (ensure controlled execution — Dormitory/Accommodation Operations, Occupancy & Resident Welfare (PA-144.2).)
- CTL-663: check-in assignment-verified; daily occupancy reconciled to HRIS; visitor register maintained (W4325)
Cross-references: - links to VS-103 (HR), VS-138 (facilities), VS-23 (security), W4316 (assignment), W4320 (system), W4334 (move-out)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Unauthorized-occupant risk**: non-employee/unassigned person housed → liability/security; mitigated by assignment-verified check-in & access control (W4325)
- **Orphan-occupancy risk**: separated employee still housed; mitigated by HRIS-reconciled daily occupancy (W4320)

steps.activity: Warden/Housing Ops run daily front-desk operations — check-in (verify assignment W4316, signed agreement W4315, orientation, key/access issuance, bed/unit handover) and check-out (key return, inspection W4334)
Warden/Housing Ops maintain the daily log (occupancy, incidents, maintenance requests, visitor register W4325), conduct rounds, and report exceptions
Housing Ops reconcile daily occupancy to the housing system/HRIS (W4320) and escalate anomalies (unauthorized occupant, separation not released)

Automation Opportunity: - Real-time bed-availability dashboard; waitlist by priority; capacity-enforced allocation; utilization analytics
Controls: - CTL-663 (ensure controlled execution — Dormitory/Accommodation Operations, Occupancy & Resident Welfare (PA-144.2).)
- CTL-663: allocation within capacity (W4318); priority documented; gender/role-appropriate; occupancy tracked
Cross-references: - links to VS-103 (HR), VS-07/VS-04 (ops), W4314 (portfolio), W4316 (assignment), W4318 (capacity), W4320 (system)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Over-allocation risk**: beds assigned beyond capacity/safety limit → overcrowding/BFP violation; mitigated by capacity-enforced allocation (W4318)
- **Waitlist-opaque risk**: unclear waitlist order → grievance; mitigated by documented priority criteria

steps.activity: Housing Ops maintain real-time bed/unit availability by site, apply allocation priority (W4316), and manage the waitlist for over-subscribed sites
Housing Ops balance gender/role-appropriate allocation (separate quarters where required), respect capacity limits (W4318), and document assignments
Housing Ops/Finance forecast occupancy vs capacity to flag need for additional units (W4314) or cost recovery gaps, and report utilization

fields.Participants: Labor Relations (VS-84), HR (VS-103), Housing Ops, HSE (VS-24), Ethics (VS-119), Resident
fields.Trigger: Resident grievance; conflict; welfare concern; incident

Automation Opportunity: - Confidential grievance channel; case-management workflow; VS-119 integration; welfare pulse-survey
Controls: - CTL-663 (ensure controlled execution — Dormitory/Accommodation Operations, Occupancy & Resident Welfare (PA-144.2).)
- CTL-663: grievance channel confidential; harassment escalated (VS-84/VS-119); anti-retaliation monitored
Cross-references: - links to VS-84 (labor relations), VS-103 (HR), VS-119 (ethics), VS-24 (HSE), VS-88 (records), W4315 (rules/eviction)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Harassment/safety risk**: unaddressed harassment/conflict in shared housing → welfare/legal exposure; mitigated by confidential grievance + VS-84/VS-119 escalation
- **Retaliation risk**: resident penalized for reporting; mitigated by anti-retaliation (VS-119) & monitoring
System Touchpoints: - HR case mgmt (VS-103/VS-84); ethics/speak-up (VS-119); HSE (VS-24); records (VS-88)
Time Estimate: - ~1–4 hrs per case; complex cases longer

steps.activity: Warden/HR receive welfare concerns/grievances (roommate conflict, harassment, unsafe condition, mental-health), log confidentially, and acknowledge to the resident
HR/Labor Relations investigate per VS-84/VS-119 (harassment/ethics escalation), take interim protection measures, and mediate/resolve
HR/Housing Ops document outcome, enforce consequence (eviction W4315 for serious breach), and monitor for retaliation/recurrence

fields.Participants: Facilities (VS-138), Housekeeping Vendor/Staff, Housing Ops, HSE (VS-24), Contingent (VS-98)
fields.Volume: Per-site housekeeping across housed units/common areas

Automation Opportunity: - Housekeeping checklist app; SLA-completion logging; deficiency auto-work-order; hygiene inspection
Controls: - CTL-663 (ensure controlled execution — Dormitory/Accommodation Operations, Occupancy & Resident Welfare (PA-144.2).)
- CTL-663: housekeeping standard met; vendor SLA-governed (W4330); hygiene inspected (HSE)
Cross-references: - links to VS-138 (FM), VS-34 (vendor), VS-24 (HSE), VS-98 (contingent), W4329 (maintenance), W4330 (vendor SLA)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Hygiene/health risk**: poor sanitation → resident illness/DOLE-OSH issue; mitigated by hygiene standard & inspection
- **Vendor-SLA risk**: outsourced housekeeping underperforms; mitigated by SLA governance (W4330)
System Touchpoints: - Facilities/FM (VS-138); housekeeping vendor (VS-34); HSE (VS-24); contingent (VS-98); maintenance (W4329)

steps.activity: Housing Ops/Facilities set the housekeeping standard & schedule — common-area cleaning frequency, sanitation, linen/laundry, waste removal, pest control (VS-138) — per HSE hygiene
Housekeeping staff/vendor execute the schedule, log completion, and report deficiencies/maintenance needs (W4329)
Housing Ops/HSE inspect hygiene/sanitation vs standard, enforce vendor SLA (W4330), and remediate deficiencies

fields.Owner: Housing Ops / Loss Prevention (VS-23) / Security Vendor
fields.Participants: LP (VS-23), Security Vendor/Guards (VS-98), Housing Ops, HSE (VS-24), Facilities (VS-138)
fields.Trigger: Housing operation; visitor arrival; security event

Automation Opportunity: - Card/biometric access tied to occupancy; visitor e-register; CCTV incident-flag; security incident workflow
Controls: - CTL-663: 24/7 access control; visitor register; CCTV privacy-compliant (VS-91); incidents investigated (VS-23)
Cross-references: - links to VS-23 (LP), VS-27.3 (access security), VS-91 (privacy), VS-98 (guards), VS-138 (FM), W4320 (system), W4327 (emergency)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Theft/intrusion risk**: unauthorized access → resident property loss/safety; mitigated by access control + 24/7 guard + CCTV
- **Visitor-abuse risk**: uncontrolled visitors → disruption/safety; mitigated by visitor registration & hours
System Touchpoints: - LP/security (VS-23); access control (VS-27.3/VS-138); CCTV privacy (VS-91); contingent (VS-98); facilities (VS-138)

steps.activity: Housing Ops/LP set the housing security standard — 24/7 guarding, access control (key/card/biometric per W4320), visitor registration & hours, CCTV (privacy per VS-91), and emergency contact
Security guards/vendor execute access control, log visitors, monitor CCTV, and respond to incidents (theft, intrusion, dispute) per VS-23
LP/Housing Ops review security incidents, investigate theft/loss, and enforce consequence/vendor SLA

fields.Participants: Facilities (VS-138), Finance (VS-17.4), Utility Providers, Telecom (VS-27), Energy (VS-120/VS-108), Sustainability (VS-25)

Automation Opportunity: - Utility sub-metering & fair-use billing; abnormal-consumption alert; outage notification; energy-efficiency analytics (VS-120)
Controls: - CTL-663 (ensure controlled execution — Dormitory/Accommodation Operations, Occupancy & Resident Welfare (PA-144.2).)
- CTL-663: utility cost allocated per model (W4317); fair-use enforced; backup power available (VS-138)
Cross-references: - links to VS-138 (facilities), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-120/VS-108 (energy), VS-27 (telecom), VS-25 (sustainability), W4317 (cost)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Cost-overrun risk**: uncontrolled utility consumption (AC overuse) → cost leak; mitigated by fair-use policy & resident share
- **Outage risk**: utility outage → resident welfare/disruption; mitigated by backup (generator per VS-138) & restoration SLA
Time Estimate: - Bill processing monthly ~hours; outage response variable

steps.activity: Facilities/Housing Ops provision utilities (water, electricity, internet/Wi-Fi) per site, establish accounts, and set conservation/fair-use rules
Finance/Housing Ops process utility bills, allocate cost per the cost model (W4317) including resident share/fair-use, and detect abnormal consumption
Housing Ops/Facilities manage outages/restoration, sustainability/energy-efficiency (VS-120) opportunities, and resident communication

fields.Participants: HSE (VS-24), Occupational Health (VS-83), BFP, Housing Ops, Insurance (VS-26), BCP (VS-26), HR (VS-103)

Automation Opportunity: - Evacuation-drill scheduler; emergency-notification to residents; contagion-alert workflow; BCP integration
Controls: - CTL-663 (ensure controlled execution — Dormitory/Accommodation Operations, Occupancy & Resident Welfare (PA-144.2).)
- CTL-663: BFP evacuation plan & drills; medical/contagion response (VS-83); emergencies insured (VS-26)
Cross-references: - links to VS-24 (HSE), VS-83 (health), VS-26 (insurance/BCP), VS-69 (disaster), VS-21.2 (risk), W4318 (safety), W4333 (fire/life-safety)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Fire/mass-casualty risk**: dormitory fire with inadequate evacuation → mass casualty; mitigated by BFP evacuation plan + drills
- **Contagion risk**: infectious disease spreading in shared quarters; mitigated by contagion-control & health response
System Touchpoints: - HSE (VS-24); occupational health (VS-83); insurance/BCP (VS-26); disaster (VS-69); risk (VS-21.2)

steps.activity: HSE/Housing Ops set the dormitory emergency plan — evacuation routes/assemblies, fire response, first-aid/medical, wardens/marshals, and resident orientation & drills (BFP/OSH)
Occupational Health/HSE provide resident medical support (clinic referral VS-83, first-aid, mental-health VS-83.3) and manage infectious-disease/contagion control in shared quarters

steps.a: HSE Mgr / Head of Internal Audit & Risk
steps.activity: HSE/Insurance/BCP manage emergencies (fire, medical, natural disaster VS-69), evacuate/restore, file insurance (VS-26), and feed BCP/risk (VS-26/VS-21.2)

fields.Participants: HR/EX (VS-103), People Analytics (VS-103.3), Housing Ops, Store/DC Ops (VS-07/VS-04), Strategy (VS-33)

Automation Opportunity: - Housing-satisfaction pulse; retention-attribution analytics; retention-ROI dashboard; action-tracking
Controls: - CTL-663 (ensure controlled execution — Dormitory/Accommodation Operations, Occupancy & Resident Welfare (PA-144.2).)
- CTL-663: housing impact measured; retention-ROI quantified; improvement actions tracked
Cross-references: - links to VS-103 (HR/EX), VS-103.3 (people analytics), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-33 (strategy), VS-141 (commute), W4313 (strategy), W4336 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Value-unknown risk**: housing cost incurred without evidence of retention impact; mitigated by retention-ROI analysis
- **Dissatisfaction risk**: poor housing experience undermines retention; mitigated by pulse & action

steps.activity: HR/EX measure housed-employee experience (housing-satisfaction pulse, commute+housing as retention drivers vs VS-141), and segment by site/role
HR/Ops analyze housing impact on retention/turnover (do housed employees stay longer?), and quantify the retention value vs housing cost
HR/Housing Ops act on findings (improve housing, expand coverage where retention-ROI positive) and feed strategy (W4313)
